item.description: Trump expressed dissatisfaction with a new Iran proposal. US Iran Ceasefire News LIVE: Trump Says 'Not Satisfied' With New Iran Proposal NDTV.

item.title: US to Withdraw 5,000 Troops From Germany as Tensions With NATO Allies Escalate Over Iran War
item.description: The US will withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany as tensions with NATO allies escalate. US to Withdraw 5,000 Troops From Germany as Tensions With NATO Allies Escalate Over Iran War Quiver Quantitative.

item.title: US Withdrawing 5,000 Troops From Germany
item.description: The US is withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany over six to twelve months. The Pentagon said the withdrawal was expected to be completed over the next six to twelve months.

item.title: Trump Tells US Congress Hostilities In Iran "Have Terminated"
item.description: President Donald Trump told Congress that hostilities in Iran have terminated. President Donald Trump told top US lawmakers on Friday that hostilities in Iran had ended, after coming under pressure from Congress to seek authorization for the conflict as it headed into its third month.

item.title: Israel Said to Have Helped Defend Emirates in Iran War With Iron Dome
item.description: Israel reportedly helped defend the UAE with its Iron Dome missile defense system during the Iran war. The Emirates bore the brunt of Iran's retaliatory attacks on Gulf countries. It appeared to be the first time the missile defense system was sent to an Arab country.

item.title: Lebanon says 12 killed in Israeli strikes on southern town
item.description: Israeli strikes killed 12 people in southern Lebanon, despite a ceasefire and evacuation warnings. Lebanon said Israeli strikes killed 12 people in the south, including in a town under an evacuation warning despite a ceasefire.

item.title: At least 12 killed in latest Israeli attacks on Lebanon
item.description: Israeli attacks on Lebanon killed at least 12, with over 2,600 dead since March 2. Israel's strikes continue, with more than 2,600 killed since March 2, despite an ongoing ceasefire.

item.title: Trump tells Congress ceasefire means he does not need their approval for Iran war
item.description: US President Trump claims congressional approval is no longer needed for a war with Iran, citing a ceasefire as proof hostilities have terminated. He made the statement in a letter to Congress on 10 April 2026.

item.title: Trump ‘Not Satisfied’ With Iran’s Proposal on Ending War
item.description: President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's proposal to end the war. The details of the latest plan were unclear, and President Trump did not specify his objections. Trump ‘Not Satisfied’ With Iran’s Proposal on Ending War.

item.description: Civil society groups are pushing the EU to sanction Kyrgyzstan. Civil society pushes EU to broaden Kyrgyzstan sanctions over alleged Russia supply route BLiTZ - Fears None But God.

item.description: The War Powers Act deadline for the Iran war is here. The act requires presidential reporting. A deadline for the Iran war is here. What does the War Powers Act say?

item.title: US judge bars Trump from ending protected status for Yemeni nationals
item.description: A US judge has blocked the Trump administration from ending protected status for Yemeni nationals, part of a broader immigration crackdown. The administration had sought to cancel temporary protections for 13 countries.

item.title: Suspect in UK Stabbing Attack on Jewish Men Faces Third Attempted Murder Charge
item.description: A man faces attempted murder charges for stabbing two Jewish men in London. A man appeared in court charged with the attempted murder of two Jewish men in Golders Green, in north London, and of another man, an acquaintance, elsewhere in the city.

item.title: Trump expands Cuba sanctions with global reach, targeting foreign banks and firms
item.description: Trump expanded Cuba sanctions to target foreign banks and firms globally. Trump expands Cuba sanctions with global reach, targeting foreign banks and firms South China Morning Post.

item.title: US Catholic Archdiocese To Pay $800 Million To Settle 1,300 Sex Abuse Cases
item.description: The US Catholic Archdiocese will pay $800 million to settle 1,300 sex abuse cases. The settlement is second only to the $880 million deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024.

item.title: In Packed Cafes, Iranians Yearn to Escape War’s Wreckage
item.description: Iranians gather in cafes to discuss hopes and fears amid uncertain times. Cafes and coffee shops give Iranians affordable places to talk about their hopes, fears and the cost of living as well as to seek company in uncertain times.

item.title: "Why Would I Tell You That?" Trump Evades Reporter's Question On Iran Strikes
item.description: Trump evaded a reporter's question on Iran strikes, citing no reason. Iran has maintained its stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, cutting off vast amounts of oil. "Why Would I Tell You That?" Trump Evades Reporter's Question On Iran Strikes.

item.title: US Military-Run Mission For Gaza Aid Set To Close Soon: Report
item.description: The US military-run Gaza aid mission is set to close soon. US officials have privately described the move as an overhaul. US Military-Run Mission For Gaza Aid Set To Close Soon: Report.

item.title: US Warns Shippers Against Paying Hormuz Toll, Threatens Sanctions Risks
item.description: The US warned shippers against paying tolls in the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most strategically vital maritime routes. US Warns Shippers Against Paying Hormuz Toll, Threatens Sanctions Risks.

item.title: U.S.'s Hormuz coalition 'not in competition' with France, U.K.-led bid: French FM
item.description: France's foreign minister said the US Hormuz coalition is not competing with theirs. The U. K. and France have led talks on a separate maritime effort, recently holding a meeting with more than 50 countries.
